title: Trust and Safety Standard: Account Recovery for Harborline Customer Accounts
content:
# Account recovery

**Product:** Harborline Customer Accounts

## Standard

1. A customer who has lost access to the sign-in email or the two-factor method may request recovery through one of the tier's recovery methods: the email link, sent to the profile contact email; PIN and card, proving the support PIN together with the last four card digits and billing postal code; or government ID, reviewed by Trust and Safety.
2. A recovery request may be submitted only when the account's recovery requests of the trailing 30 days are fewer than the tier's maximum, and no rejection was decided in the last cooldown period of calendar days. The requests counted are those whose submission date falls in the trailing 30 calendar days ending today, today included, whatever their outcome.
3. Trust and Safety decides each request within the tier's review time in business days, counted Monday to Friday excluding US federal holidays, and an approved request puts the account in recovery hold.
4. The approved reset may take effect only at or after the moment the recovery request was approved plus the tier's recovery hold hours elapsed. The hold is counted in full 24-hour periods of elapsed time from the approval moment, never in calendar days. The account records the moment the waiting period ends.
5. During recovery hold the holder cannot change security settings, withdraw credit, close the account or obtain a domain authorisation code, while renewals and auto-renew charges continue.
6. A request withdrawn by the holder before the hold ends releases the hold without applying the reset.
7. Every approval, rejection and applied reset is notified to the previous and current sign-in emails where the tier's security notice setting is on. When the waiting period ends and the approved reset takes effect, the account returns to active and the change to the sign-in email or the two-factor method is recorded on the account as a security change, with its security-change notice.

## Figures by tier

| Tier | Recovery methods accepted | Review time (business days) | Recovery hold (elapsed hours) | Requests allowed in a trailing 30 days | Cooldown after a rejection (calendar days) | Notice to the previous sign-in email |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Harborline Personal Account | email link, PIN and card, government ID | 2 | 72 | 3 | 7 | Yes (true) |
| Harborline Business Account | email link, PIN and card, government ID | 2 | 72 | 3 | 7 | Yes (true) |
| Harborline Reseller Bronze | PIN and card, government ID | 1 | 96 | 3 | 7 | Yes (true) |
| Harborline Reseller Silver | PIN and card, government ID | 1 | 96 | 3 | 7 | Yes (true) |
| Harborline Reseller Gold | government ID | 1 | 120 | 3 | 7 | Yes (true) |
| Harborline Reseller Platinum | government ID | 1 | 120 | 3 | 7 | Yes (true) |

## Hold boundary (hypothetical moments)

A request on a Harborline Personal Account is approved at 14:20 on a Tuesday. Seventy-two elapsed hours later is 14:20 on the Friday. The reset may take effect at 14:20 on the Friday or later; at 14:19 on the Friday it may not, even though Friday is the third calendar day after the approval.

## Submission test (hypothetical)

An account already shows three recovery requests submitted in the trailing 30 days, one rejected and two withdrawn. A fourth request may not be submitted: three is not fewer than the maximum of 3, whatever the outcomes.
